news.headline: Moderna Shares Extend Rally to ~137% Over the Month Amid Short-Squeeze Dynamics
news.summary: MRNA rose another ~6% to roughly $154 on September 17, extending gains to about 137% over the prior month as short sellers (an estimated 13-14% of free float) continued covering positions after the August 19 melanoma-vaccine data. William Blair upgraded the stock to Outperform and Leerink Partners raised its peak sales estimate for intismeran autogene to roughly $1.4 billion by 2032.

news.headline: FDA Approves Moderna's Updated 2026-2027 Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE COVID-19 Vaccines
news.summary: On August 27, 2026 the FDA approved the JN.1-lineage XFG-subvariant 2026-2027 formulas of Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE; Spikevax is cleared for ages 6 months-64 with a high-risk condition plus all adults 65+, while mNEXSPIKE covers ages 12-64 with a high-risk condition plus adults 65+. The narrower age-based labels (versus prior universal recommendations) keep both shots restricted mainly to high-risk and older populations.

news.headline: Merck and Moderna's mRNA Melanoma Vaccine Hits Both Endpoints in Phase 3 INTerpath-001 Trial
news.summary: Intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940) combined with Merck's Keytruda met both co-primary/key endpoints - recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival - in the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial of resected stage IIB-IV melanoma, the first positive late-stage trial for an individualized mRNA cancer vaccine. Moderna shares nearly doubled intraday on the news, and the companies said they aim to file for regulatory approval within months.

news.headline: FDA Approves mFlusiva, Moderna's First mRNA-Based Flu Vaccine, but ACIP Recommendation Remains Stalled
news.summary: The FDA approved mFlusiva (mRNA-1010) on August 5, 2026 for adults 50-64 and 65+, Moderna's fifth approved product and the first mRNA seasonal flu vaccine, conditional on an additional post-approval trial in the 65+ group; in trials it showed about 27% greater relative efficacy than a standard-dose flu shot. A March 2026 federal court ruling has left ACIP unable to issue new recommendations, meaning insurers are not required to cover mFlusiva and its fall 2026-27 rollout is at risk.

news.headline: Moderna Q2 2026 Revenue Beats Guidance at $145M; Narrows 2026 Cost Guidance After $950M Patent Settlement Payment
news.summary: Q2 2026 revenue was $145 million versus a guided range of $50-100 million, with a roughly $782 million GAAP net loss partly reflecting the $950 million upfront payment in Moderna's LNP patent settlement with Genevant/Arbutus. Moderna reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of up to 10% growth while cutting cost-of-sales guidance to $1.7 billion (from $1.8 billion) and R&D guidance to $2.9 billion (from $3.0 billion).

news.headline: Moderna's Norovirus Vaccine Misses Phase 3 Interim Efficacy Bar; Trial Extended With New Cohort
news.summary: Moderna disclosed on July 31, 2026 that its trivalent norovirus candidate mRNA-1403 did not meet the statistical bar for early success in its Phase 3 interim analysis because too few norovirus infections had occurred among the roughly 20,000-25,000 enrollees; the company is recruiting an additional cohort to assess efficacy through the 2026-2027 winter season. Shares fell about 5.7%-7% intraday despite management maintaining its overall growth targets.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: Financial-data aggregators list Moderna's Q3 2026 results around late October to early November 2026 (estimates range from Oct 29 to Nov 5), though the company has not yet published an official date. The release should update 2026-27 respiratory-season uptake for mFlusiva, Spikevax, mNEXSPIKE and mRESVIA, progress on the norovirus vaccine's expanded cohort, and full-year revenue/cost guidance.

catalysts.label: Intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157) regulatory filing for melanoma
catalysts.detail: Following the August 19, 2026 Phase 3 INTerpath-001 success, Moderna and Merck said they intend to file for approval with global regulators (including the FDA) within months, without giving a specific date, and will present full data at an upcoming international medical meeting. Approval would mark the first individualized mRNA cancer therapy to reach market.

catalysts.label: ACIP reconvening and vote on mFlusiva coverage recommendation
catalysts.detail: A March 2026 federal court ruling left the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices unable to issue new vaccine recommendations, so mFlusiva currently lacks an ACIP recommendation that insurers typically rely on for no-cost coverage. Moderna has said the vaccine could still become broadly available this fall if the legal impasse is resolved and ACIP reconvenes in time for the 2026-27 flu season.

catalysts.label: mRNA-1403 norovirus vaccine expanded-cohort Phase 3 readout
catalysts.detail: After the initial interim analysis fell short due to insufficient norovirus infections in the study population, Moderna is enrolling an additional participant cohort to re-assess vaccine efficacy over the 2026-2027 winter norovirus season. A successful readout would support Moderna's push to diversify beyond respiratory vaccines.

catalysts.label: mCOMBRIAX (flu/COVID combination vaccine) US regulatory path
catalysts.detail: mCOMBRIAX has EU marketing authorization, but Moderna withdrew its original U.S. FDA application in May 2025 pending additional Phase 3 data and has not given an updated U.S. filing timeline. A renewed U.S. submission, if and when filed, would be a first-of-its-kind combination shot for the American market.

catalysts.label: Potential broader COVID-19 vaccine label via Phase 4 data
catalysts.detail: Moderna is working with the FDA on post-marketing (Phase 4) data for Spikevax/mNEXSPIKE aimed at restoring eligibility to a wider population than the current high-risk/65+-focused label the agency imposed. Any label expansion would be a meaningful catalyst for core COVID vaccine volumes, but no submission or decision date has been disclosed.

pulse: MRNA trades around $154 (Sept 19, 2026, intraday range roughly $150-$160) within a 52-week band of $22.28-$176.66, having rallied over 100% since the August 19 Phase 3 INTerpath-001 melanoma cancer-vaccine win with Merck, a move amplified by heavy short covering (short interest estimated at 13-14% of float). Near-term narrative is split between oncology momentum - intismeran autogene's expected regulatory filing 'within months' - and respiratory-franchise headwinds, as newly FDA-approved products (mFlusiva flu shot, updated Spikevax/mNEXSPIKE COVID shots) face an ACIP recommendation vacuum that threatens insurance coverage and fall 2026-27 uptake even as core COVID/RSV vaccine revenue keeps shrinking. Cost discipline continues (2026 cost-of-sales and R&D guidance both trimmed at Q2), while the norovirus vaccine's Phase 3 miss underscores execution risk in the pipeline-diversification push.
